summaries.demographer: Saba Guevara is a 23-year-old never-married woman living in Yuba City, California with her parents and younger brother in a rented household (Q05, Q11, Q51, Q84). She is U.S.-born, Mexican American on her mother's side and Uzbek/Central Asian on her father's side, and identifies as mixed race, Latina, and Uzbek (Q86-Q89). She has a high school diploma, is not currently enrolled in school, and works as a retail salesperson in apparel and home goods (Q90-Q92, Q65). Her household is working-class to lower-middle-income, supported by her parents' wages and her retail income, with shared expenses and limited but real savings capacity (Q55-Q58, Q72-Q74, Q83).
summaries.behavioral_economist: Saba shows pragmatic time preferences: she delayed college to avoid uncertain debt and earn income, then reframed retail as a stepping stone after receiving positive workplace feedback (Q02-Q04). She is budget-conscious but vulnerable to small impulse purchases tied to stress, fashion, and decor, which she manages through paycheck budgeting, savings goals, and spending cuts (Q50, Q60-Q64). Her choices are strongly identity-linked: career plans, travel, fashion, and business goals all combine earning potential with cultural expression (Q65, Q108). She is risk-aware rather than risk-avoidant, willing to pursue promotion and future entrepreneurship while prioritizing emergency savings and household obligations (Q61-Q63, Q82-Q83).
summaries.political_scientist: Saba is a moderate-to-strong Democratic leaner who votes by mail in major elections and increasingly attends to local politics because of rent, wages, roads, training, and public services (Q23-Q25, Q95-Q96). Her political views center on workers' pay, health care affordability, immigration, reproductive rights, LGBTQ inclusion, and practical policy delivery (Q24). She supports Black Lives Matter concerns about accountability and unequal treatment while engaging mainly through conversations, small donations, and workplace behavior rather than protest participation (Q26-Q30). Her institutional trust is selective: she trusts doctors and public health sources more than viral posts, and views politicians and police with pragmatic skepticism (Q20-Q21, Q24, Q42).
summaries.psychologist: Saba presents as ambitious, socially grounded, and creatively observant, with a self-concept built around family responsibility, independence, and making ordinary spaces beautiful (Q01, Q43, Q109). She experiences situational anxiety around money, career progress, and comparison, but reports no diagnosed depression or anxiety and generally maintains functioning through work, walks, cooking, planning, and close relationships (Q43-Q45, Q50). Her coping style is practical and relational: she talks to her mother or close friends, creates lists, budgets, and returns to concrete tasks after stress (Q43-Q46). She is skeptical but open, balancing immigrant-family work ethic and hospitality with a young adult desire for autonomy, travel, education, and creative entrepreneurship (Q37, Q47, Q83, Q108).
